author: Contributor 86
about: Trailmark, a two-person startup selling branded short links with a partner program, over its first half-year on PlanetScale: Maya sets up the database, its passwords and service tokens, a migration job creates and changes the schema through @planetscale/database with an admin password and backs the branch up before each change, the application counts clicks, imports campaigns and runs monthly partner payouts with a read/write password, and in June the program closes and Trailmark exports its data and deletes the database. Credentials are captured as opaque values: https://planetscale.com/docs/vitess/connecting/connection-strings documents a unique username and password pair, and https://planetscale.com/docs/vitess/tutorials/planetscale-serverless-driver names <PS_USERNAME> without a hexadecimal format or fixed length. Empty query results and an update matching no rows are checked on the wire, where psdb's JSON leaves a field at its default value out (https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json/), and as @planetscale/database decodes them (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/planetscale/database-js/v1.19.0/src/index.ts). The signup password is a public fixture created and reused only in this World.

and the Read/Write password app, whose username and password go into Vercel's environment
